messages.subject: Prediction at validation stations
parts:
Hello,

I would like to estimate a INLA model at 100 training stations and validate the model at 50 validation stations, which should be excluded from the training data set. Furthermore, for each station 20 observations are available in the training and validation data. 
Unfortunately, I really struggle with it and I can not make it run. The code produces an error message including a hint, but somehow I can not make it work. I attached the code producing the error for replication. I am also not sure, if I specified the objects A_train/A_val and stack_train/stack_val correctly in the code. 
I would really appreciate if you help me! Thank you so much!!!!!!

library(INLA)
###########################################
# ARTIFICAL EXAMPLE
###########################################
set.seed(123)

# number of observations (obs) for each location (loc)
t <- 20

# sample n = 100 locations to train
n <- 100
loc_train <- t(sapply(1:n, function(k) c(runif(1, 0, 5), runif(1, 0, 10))))
colnames(loc_train) <- c("x", "y")
# training data set including number of observation t, grid point (x, y),
# observation (obs) and covariate (cov)
df.loc_train <- data.frame(t = rep(1:t, each = nrow(loc_train)),
                           loc_train,
                           obs = rnorm(t*nrow(loc_train)),
                           cov = rnorm(t*nrow(loc_train)))

# sample n = 50 locations to validate
n <- 50
loc_val <- t(sapply(1:n, function(k) c(runif(1, 0, 5), runif(1, 0, 10))))
colnames(loc_val) <- c("x", "y")
# validation data set including number of observation t, grid point (x, y),
# observation (obs) and covariate (cov)
df.loc_val <- data.frame(t = rep(1:t, each = nrow(loc_val)),
                         loc_val,
                         obs = rnorm(t*nrow(loc_val)),
                         cov = rnorm(t*nrow(loc_val)))

# construct mesh for training locations
mesh <- inla.mesh.create(loc = loc_train,
                         cutoff = 0,
                         refine = list(max.edge = 10, min.angle = 0.01))
plot(mesh)
points(x = loc_train[, 1], y = loc_train[, 2], col = "red")
points(x = loc_val[, 1], y = loc_val[, 2], col = "blue")

# create spde
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh,
                          alpha = 2)

field.indices <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "field",
                                      n.spde = mesh$n,
                                      n.repl = t)

# observation matrix A for the training locations
A_train <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh,
                            loc = loc_train,
                            index = rep(1:nrow(loc_train), times = t),
                            repl = rep(1:t, each = nrow(loc_train)))

# observation matrix A for the validation locations
A_val <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh,
                          loc = loc_val,
                          index = rep(1:nrow(loc_val), times = t),
                          repl = rep(1:t, each = nrow(loc_val)))


stack_train <- inla.stack(data = list(Y = df.loc_train$obs),
                          A = list(A_train, 1),
                          effects = list(field.indices,
                                         list(cov = df.loc_train$cov)),
                          tag = "train")

stack_val <- inla.stack(data = list(Y = NA),
                        A = list(A_val, 1),
                        effects = list(field.indices,
                                       list(cov = df.loc_val$cov)),
                        tag = "val")

stack <- inla.stack(stack_train, stack_val)

fit <- inla(formula = Y ~ f(field, model = spde) + f(field, cov, model = spde),
            family = "gaussian",
            data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE),
            control.inla = control.inla(strategy = "auto"),
            control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction at validation stations
parts:
Hi Peter,

your model formula has two conflicting latent component definitions.
If you wanted a model like
\eta(s) = u(s) + v(s) * cov(s)
for two independent spatial fields u and v, then you have to give the
component different names. In the plain INLA interface you need to do
that by having two differently named "field" index variables.
Also, you're constructing index variables for a temporally replicated
field, but you're not using that in the model definition, so it's not
entirely clear what model it is you're trying to implement.
If you were intending both u and v to be temporally replicated
(independent for each time point, but with time-constant covariance
parameters):

stack_train <- inla.stack(data = list(Y = df.loc_train$obs),
A = list(A_train,

Diagonal(nrow(df.loc_train), df.loc_train$cov) %*% A_train,
effects = list(field.indices, field_cov.indices),
tag = "train")

stack_val <- ...

stack <- inla.stack(stack_train, stack_val)

fit <- inla(formula = Y ~ f(field, model = spde, replicate =
field.repl) + f(field_cov, model = spde, replicate = field_cov.repl),

family = "gaussian",
data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE),
control.inla = control.inla(strategy = "auto"),
control.compute = list(config = TRUE))
